examples.question_text: Evaluate (a) $\sin25^{\circ}$, (b) $\cos52^{\circ}$ and (c) $\tan38^{\circ}$ correct to $4$ decimal places.
examples.solution_text:
Set the calculator to degree mode.

(a) $\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\sin25^{\circ}\\&=0.422618\ldots\\&\approx0.4226\end{aligned}$

(b) $\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\cos52^{\circ}\\&=0.615661\ldots\\&\approx0.6157\end{aligned}$

(c) $\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\tan38^{\circ}\\&=0.781285\ldots\\&\approx0.7813\end{aligned}$

In degree mode, evaluate the cosine and multiply by $8$. Keep full precision until the final rounding.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}8\cos32^{\circ}\\&=6.784384\ldots\\&\approx6.7844\end{aligned}$

In degree mode, evaluate the sine, then divide its value by $5$.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{\sin61^{\circ}}{5}\\&=0.174923\ldots\\&\approx0.1749\end{aligned}$

In degree mode, divide $11$ by the sine value. Keep the denominator at full precision.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{11}{\sin49^{\circ}}\\&=14.575142\ldots\\&\approx14.5751\end{aligned}$

In degree mode, evaluate the cosine, multiply by $6$, then divide by $7$. Round only the final result.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{6\cos23^{\circ}}{7}\\&=0.789004\ldots\\&\approx0.7890\end{aligned}$

In degree mode, evaluate the tangent and multiply by $4$ to obtain the whole denominator. Divide $10$ by that unrounded value.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{10}{4\tan35^{\circ}}\\&=\frac{10}{2.800830\ldots}\\&=3.570370\ldots\\&\approx3.5704\end{aligned}$
